title: One-hot encoding by broadcasting
prompt: Write `one_hot(labels, k)`: `labels` is a 1-D array of integer class labels in [0, k). Return a float array of shape (len(labels), k) with a 1.0 in each row's label column and 0.0 elsewhere. Raise `ValueError` if any label is outside [0, k). No Python loops.
hints: Compare every label with every possible class at once. What shapes broadcast to (n, k)?
`labels[:, None]` has shape (n, 1) and `np.arange(k)` has shape (k,); comparing them gives an (n, k) boolean matrix. Check the range first with `(labels < 0) | (labels >= k)`.
if np.any((labels < 0) | (labels >= k)): raise ValueError(...); return (labels[:, None] == np.arange(k)).astype(float)
